diagnosis: Both runs failed first on excessive fillet radius and then on a missing World after realize; only execution 3 rendered successfully, so neither received an executable visual correction. Repeated include keys also silently replaced objects in the initial compartment program, and mesh-name material targeting missed SceneAct parent names. Final renders retain substantial framing, coverage, silhouette and tonal differences despite passing prescribed structural/material/move checks. Baseline overall scores are 0.390749 and 0.347963. The +10% focal probe reduced the first score to 0.387274; scaling only its small trim group yielded 0.390894, insufficient evidence for whole-object scale correction. Archive arrays are empty, and omitted geometry rows are not certified by their summaries.
rationale: Recover the two visual-correction opportunities lost in each supplied trajectory by documenting actual constructor and Blender initialization constraints. Add explicit failure feedback, landmark-guided revisions, bounded orchestration and selection among observed successful builds. Correct snap/bind defaults to match the supplied implementation. Meta planning prioritizes execution failures before spending diagnostic renders and spreads eligible camera probes across development cases.
interpretation: Intervention sensitivity and later shared-code outcome are shown separately. This is not proof that the probe caused a gain; other development cases and terminal results remain necessary.
